MiniMaxH3MasterNode.purpose: Build and generate a sequence of clips from one timeline.
MiniMaxH3MasterNode.use: Start here for prompts, per-clip references, continuity, approval and clip LoRAs.
wiring: Text encoder → Master.clip; VAEs → matching VAE inputs
steps: Load the starter and select installed model, text encoder and VAE files.
Add a clip and choose its type. Assign only the references that clip needs.
Write the clip prompt. Start with one short clip and optional stages disconnected.
Choose Next clip or All clips, then run. Review the result and approve only clips you want reused.

examples.setup: Choose REF2V and select the character pictures from the connected pool. Mention the generated Picture tokens in the prompt.
examples.expect: Only assigned references become that clip’s reference inputs; unrelated pool entries do not all go to the model.

examples.setup: On clip 2 choose Motion Context, set video and audio context independently, and choose New footage duration.
examples.expect: The previous completed result supplies context. Context is removed from delivered new frames.

examples.setup: Unapprove the clip. Continuity-dependent later approvals are invalidated while their cached results remain until replacement.
examples.expect: A run regenerates the eligible clips and replaces their current results. Approved independent results remain reusable.

notes: FL2VA serves text/keyframe tasks; REF2VA serves reference/video editing tasks. Keeping both connected does not force one model for every clip.

Approval controls generation reuse. It does not decide which completed idle results Smart Preview may display. Before actual Master execution input arrives, Smart Preview can restore existing encoded media read-only; it cannot create, update or delete browser/server preview caches. Draft timeline widgets are not execution input.
Saved results contain completed latents, not persistent paused sampler state. Ten completed steps plus fifteen refinement steps is not twenty-five initial steps.
The yellow outline is selection. Saved-result indicators, approval and the active generation animation have different meanings.

Identical reruns reuse one active sampling configuration sharing native base weights. Model, adapter or sigma changes replace it. CPU adapter file reuse is bounded to 256 MiB and eight files; oversized adapters are not kept in an extra file cache. ComfyUI still controls residency and its Free Memory control clears this handle. Prompt/seed changes do not invalidate model configuration.

Clear VRAM in the always-visible Project header requests native GPU model unloading when the queue is idle. Saved clips, encoded references and project files remain. The next generation loads the model again. Clip boundaries preserve native reusable weight buffers; ComfyUI still owns end-of-node cleanup and memory-pressure eviction.

The floating Server monitor shows server CPU, GPU utilization and VRAM. Drag its header to move it; minimize to pause readings. Toggle it in ComfyUI Settings → MiniMax H3 → Monitor. Position and GPU choice persist in this browser; GPU readings include other applications on the server. Shared GPU RAM is resident GPU-accessible system memory read directly through WSL, when supported; a dash means unavailable. No SSH dependency is used.

MiniMaxH3DirectorSettings.purpose: Set the output canvas and initial sampling settings.
MiniMaxH3DirectorSettings.use: Change generation dimensions and quality settings without filling the Master with global controls.
steps: Choose Manual canvas for an explicit width and height, or Auto for megapixels plus aspect.
Keep H3 generation at 24 fps. Use dimensions on the 32-pixel grid.
Match steps and sampler to your chosen model/LoRA workflow.
Keep decoded_output at latest for normal preview use; use Project Video to export the entire cached project.

examples.setup: Try a small 320 × 192 canvas and two steps for wiring checks only.
examples.expect: Quick, low-quality output suitable for detecting integration errors, not assessing final visual quality.

examples.setup: Choose decoded_output=latest and connect Smart Preview.
examples.expect: Raw IMAGE output contains the last returned clip while cached project results remain available to Full video and export.

notes: Generation output size and reference-media size are separate controls. Reference video megapixels belong in Reference Pack.
Changing dimensions, schedule, LoRAs, attention or continuity can change output despite the same prompt and seed.
Higher steps and more pixels cost time; neither guarantees better content.

MiniMaxH3RefPack.purpose: Prepare connected reference assets once, then let each clip choose its subset.
MiniMaxH3RefPack.use: Name, trim, crop, resize and describe pictures, videos and audio supplied by loader nodes.
wiring: Load Video.VIDEO or frame batch → Reference Pack.video_1
steps: Connect media loader outputs to matching inputs. Use the Edit Reference dropdown to work on one asset at a time.
Give each reference a useful name. For video choose Video + Audio, Video Only, Audio Only or Single Frame.
Open Resize and set video input preparation, usually Megapixels with the 0.5 MP default.
Select references separately on each Master clip. Reset Settings affects the selected reference, not its source connection.

examples.goal: Use a video for motion without its sound
examples.setup: Choose Video Only for that video reference and select it on a compatible clip.
examples.expect: Its visual stream is available to the clip; the paired soundtrack is not passed as that video’s audio.

examples.setup: Choose Megapixels and 0.5 on a large video.
examples.expect: Asset preparation changes its pixel dimensions before it reaches native model reference encoding. It does not change output canvas size.

examples.setup: Choose Single Frame, trim the useful range, then set Picked Frame time relative to that trimmed range.
examples.expect: The prepared reference is an image, so clip selection follows image-type limits.

notes: Native VIDEO carries timing and may carry audio. An IMAGE frame batch carries neither soundtrack nor intrinsic FPS; supply source FPS and paired audio separately.
Roles and Prompt Cast guide prompt writing. They do not replace clip reference selection or automatically force model endpoints.
No Add Pack Files or manual Refresh References button is needed: connect loader nodes; the editor watches connections and loader changes.
A bigger pool does not increase one clip’s allowed reference counts.
Each pack has four image, two video and two standalone audio sockets. Chain another pack for more connected media; clip limits still apply.
Native reference conditioning limits videos to 15 seconds each and 15 seconds total, and audio to 15 seconds each and 15 seconds total. Trim long sources before assignment.

At Master run start, connected image, video and audio inputs are prepared using native H3 sizing and stored as CPU RefMod-format safetensors in the project reference_latents folder. Matching encodes are reused across clips and later runs; disconnected assets lose their derived cache entries. Input content, preparation, native H3 code and VAE identity affect reuse. Unknown modified VAEs conservatively use a session identity. Preparing an input does not select it for clip conditioning.

MiniMaxH3SmartPreview.purpose: Review the latest completed clip or the current full sequence in the browser.
MiniMaxH3SmartPreview.use: Watch results update after each completed clip without exporting the entire movie after every run.
steps: Connect the project_state output from the Master you want to inspect.
Choose Latest clip to review one result, or Full video to inspect the sequence and its joins.
Use the stage selector for available First Pass or Refine stages; keep Final Output for the normal result.
Choose preview resolution, autoplay and Save preview as needed. These do not change generation settings.

examples.goal: Review a four-clip run as it progresses
examples.setup: Leave the preview connected and choose Full video.
examples.expect: Queuing alone preserves the old preview. Once a predecessor is successfully replaced, its continuity-dependent successors lose their old cached files and approvals. Regenerated successors appear as they finish; independent clips remain.

examples.setup: Leave Autoplay off.
examples.expect: Completed media is prebuffered when feasible. Browser storage is best effort and bounded; large files may stream instead.

examples.setup: Open the same workflow/project and connected preview.
examples.expect: Preferences and playback position for the same revision can be restored. A regenerated revision loads fresh media rather than an older position.

notes: The preview reads current server-side results. Approval is a Master reuse decision, not a requirement for viewing a completed result.
Saved Take history is removed. Regeneration replaces the current result and evicts superseded preview revisions.
Original Resolution preserves generation dimensions; 540p/720p/1080p are playback caps, not model settings.
Browser cache cannot restore deleted server latents, and a preview MP4 is not a continuation checkpoint.

Starting All clips preserves the old preview until a successful replacement. Replacing a predecessor deletes its continuity-dependent successors’ cached results; independent/source clips stop that chain. Both scopes prebuffer completed revisions with autoplay off.

Playback can start while clips are still downloading. Full Video reuses the same per-clip video fragments as Latest Clip, with one joined soundtrack to preserve audio fades and gain matching. Save preview remains a separate downloadable MP4. Browsers without supported MediaSource playback fall back to ordinary MP4 streaming.
Continuity prefixes and visible PCM are resampled together before the join, avoiding separate resampler edges at the cut. This helps seam artifacts, not poor audio generated within a clip.

Save preview explicitly downloads the displayed scope and revision through ComfyUI authentication, with progress and error feedback. A scope/revision change while downloading does not change which result that download saves.

project_state.what: Master project state with project identity and clips
project_state.when: Connect the Master you want Smart Preview to follow.
project_state.effect: Carries STRING data to this operation.
project_state.caution: Use a matching output type and compatible media/model family.

contract.name: project_state
contract.description: Connect the Master's project_state output. Reads completed shot caches without exporting the full movie.

MiniMaxH3DirectorSelfLift.use: Experiment with generation cost after you have a working full-resolution baseline.
wiring: Learned H3 latent upscaler must be installed and selected
steps: Keep the same prompt, references, seed and target canvas for a baseline with SelfLift disconnected.
Connect SelfLift and select a compatible learned H3 latent upscaler.
Choose lowres_scale and the split: final highres_steps or an explicit transition_step.
Review fine details and motion against the baseline before adopting it for a sequence.

examples.setup: With 20 initial steps and highres_steps=4, early work runs small and the last four run at target size.
examples.expect: This is one staged initial generation, not a separate Refine pass.

examples.setup: Use a less aggressive lowres_scale or more final high-resolution steps.
examples.expect: More work happens at target resolution; details may recover better, at additional cost.

notes: SelfLift can alter faces, hands, framing and motion. It is an optional tradeoff, not a guaranteed speed or quality improvement.

rho adds a pixel-anchor path with extra decode/encode work.
SelfLift runs before Refine. Reference Pack megapixels resize conditioning media, not this generation canvas.

lowres_scale.what: The spatial size ratio for SelfLift’s early steps.
lowres_scale.when: Try it after a full-resolution baseline is working.
lowres_scale.effect: 0.5 means half width and half height, roughly one quarter of the pixels for early work.
lowres_scale.caution: Aggressive reduction can lose facial, hand and motion detail.

contract.name: lowres_scale

highres_steps.what: The final initial-generation steps evaluated at target resolution.

contract.name: highres_steps
contract.description: Number of final steps to evaluate at full canvas resolution.

native_low_carry.what: Reuse low-resolution context for SelfLift continuations.
native_low_carry.when: Use when consecutive clips are generated with a compatible SelfLift continuity setup.

contract.name: native_low_carry
contract.description: Carry over low-res context frames across multi-segment continuity.

split_mode.what: How SelfLift chooses the low-to-high-resolution transition.
split_mode.when: Choose a count of final highres_steps or an explicit transition_step.
split_mode.effect: Activates one of the two split controls.
split_mode.caution: The two values do not independently add steps.

transition_step.what: The explicit point at which SelfLift lifts to high resolution.
transition_step.effect: Moves work between the low-resolution and target-resolution portions.

sampler_mode.caution: Follow does not make incompatible samplers supported.

rho.when: Leave zero initially; experiment when you need to preserve the low-resolution structure at the lift.

w_min.when: Adjust only after testing the rho anchor path.

w_max.when: Adjust only after testing the rho anchor path.
w_max.effect: Changes how the anchor contribution is weighted.
w_max.caution: These are not LoRA strengths or CFG values.

latent_upsample.what: Interpolation used by the SelfLift latent preparation path.
latent_upsample.when: Compare bilinear and nearest if the transition creates unwanted smoothing or texture.

latent_upsample.caution: This does not replace the required learned H3 upscaler.

enable_tiling.effect: More/smaller tiles trade working memory for repeated work; overlap helps boundary blending.
enable_tiling.caution: Not a hard memory cap. Tiles can change numerical behavior and require sufficient overlap.

tile_count.what: Split spatial work into overlapping tiles on the supported stage.

tile_overlap.effect: More/smaller tiles trade working memory for repeated work; overlap helps boundary blending.
tile_overlap.caution: Not a hard memory cap. Tiles can change numerical behavior and require sufficient overlap.

model_hires.when: Connect a different supported model only when deliberately changing high-resolution or refinement behavior.

MiniMaxH3DirectorRefine.purpose: Rework a generated clip, optionally enlarging it first.
MiniMaxH3DirectorRefine.use: Review a completed first pass before spending additional time on refinement.
steps: Choose refine for the same resolution, upscale for enlargement plus diffusion, or latent_upscale for preparation without diffusion.
Start with one pass and modest denoise. Steps are extra work after initial generation.
Enable Confirm First Pass before the initial run if you want to inspect it before refining.
Review the first pass, approve that stage on the timeline card, then run again to finish refinement without repeating an unchanged first pass.

examples.goal: Preserve sound while trying visual refinement

examples.expect: Video is refined while first-pass audio is retained; improvement is not guaranteed.

examples.setup: Use mode=upscale, canvas_policy=follow and choose megapixels.
examples.expect: A target canvas is derived from the actual first-pass aspect and snapped to H3 dimensions before refinement.

examples.setup: Use Confirm First Pass to review an initial result, then a separate refinement pass.
examples.expect: This is not equivalent to twenty-five initial steps. Exact persistent sampler resume is not exposed.

global retains first-pass audio. sampler refines the joint audiovisual latent, so sound can change.
A previously completed clip without a matching staged first pass is not automatically a refinement-only source.
Strong denoise or repeated passes can change identity, motion and flicker. Compare First Pass and Final Output.
The memory planner is an estimate, not a guaranteed hard VRAM cap. Skip FL2V protects endpoints by default.

enabled.when: Turn off for a baseline, or on when you want its extra processing.
enabled.effect: Disabled leaves the stage out of generation.
enabled.caution: Connecting a modifier does not prove it improved the output; compare results.

contract.name: enabled
contract.description: Toggle 2nd-pass refinement

mode.caution: Target dimensions do not affect same-resolution refine.

contract.name: mode

contract.name: steps

contract.name: denoise

contract.name: target_width
contract.description: Target upscale width

target_height.what: The pixel dimensions used by this stage.
target_height.when: Choose an explicit delivery or generation size when its canvas policy uses manual dimensions.
target_height.effect: More pixels increase processing and memory; aspect mismatch may stretch, crop or pad according to the selected policy.

contract.name: target_height

enable_tiling.what: Split spatial work into overlapping tiles on the supported stage.
enable_tiling.when: Use when the full canvas exceeds practical memory, then inspect tile boundaries.

tile_count.what: Split spatial work into overlapping tiles on the supported stage.

scheduler.what: The integration method and noise-level schedule.
scheduler.when: Use the combination required by the model/LoRA or the reference workflow you are matching.
scheduler.effect: Changes the sampling path, so the same seed may produce a different clip.
scheduler.caution: SelfLift supports only its validated Euler-compatible paths; arbitrary samplers are not interchangeable.

memory_budget_mb.caution: Zero uses automatic behavior. The estimate is not a guaranteed peak-memory limit.

upscale_precision.what: Numerical precision for supported upscale preparation.
upscale_precision.when: Keep auto initially; choose a supported precision for a specific memory or numerical need.
upscale_precision.effect: Lower precision can reduce memory while changing numerical error.
upscale_precision.caution: Hardware and model compatibility still apply.

confirm_first_pass.what: Pause for review after initial generation, before refinement.
confirm_first_pass.when: Enable before generating when you want to inspect the first pass and refine later.

contract.description: Pause after the initial pass; approve it on its timeline card, then run refinement without repeating initial sampling.

contract.description: Skip refinement for first-and-last-frame clips to protect their endpoints.

contract.description: Experimental learned latent burn-signature correction. Off by default.

guard_sensitivity.when: Leave off unless you have diagnosed that specific artifact and are comparing the correction.
guard_sensitivity.effect: Controls which signatures are corrected and by how much.
guard_sensitivity.caution: It is not a general-purpose quality enhancer or an anatomy repair tool.

guard_strength.what: Experimental correction for learned latent-upscale burn signatures.
guard_strength.when: Leave off unless you have diagnosed that specific artifact and are comparing the correction.
guard_strength.effect: Controls which signatures are corrected and by how much.
guard_strength.caution: It is not a general-purpose quality enhancer or an anatomy repair tool.

refine_model.what: An optional compatible model for this stage.
refine_model.when: Connect a different supported model only when deliberately changing high-resolution or refinement behavior.
refine_model.effect: Overrides the normal model for that stage.
refine_model.caution: MODEL socket compatibility alone does not prove H3 family/weight compatibility.

contract.name: refine_model
contract.description: Optional alternative UNET model for the second pass (e.g. non-turbo model).

sigmas.when: Override this stage’s generated schedule for controlled advanced sampling.
sigmas.effect: Carries SIGMAS data to this operation.
sigmas.caution: Use a matching output type and compatible media/model family.

refine_seed.what: The random seed for this stage.
refine_seed.when: Keep fixed for controlled comparisons; use a different seed for another attempt.
refine_seed.caution: The same seed alone is not enough for identical output: model, schedule, references and continuity must match too.

contract.name: refine_seed
contract.description: Unsigned 64-bit decimal seed; only used by Independent.

canvas_policy.effect: Chooses which dimensions or pixel budget are active.

contract.description: Workspace headroom after managed weights and device reservations. A heuristic, not a guaranteed peak VRAM limit.

guard_mode.effect: Controls which signatures are corrected and by how much.
guard_mode.caution: It is not a general-purpose quality enhancer or an anatomy repair tool.

contract.description: Correct the learned burn direction only, or positive and negative outliers.

seed_after_generate.what: How the independent refine seed advances after success.
seed_after_generate.when: Use fixed for comparisons, or increment/decrement/randomize for later refinement attempts.
seed_after_generate.effect: Updates only the independent refine seed.
seed_after_generate.caution: It does not advance the clip’s initial seed.

Describe the intended face appearance without requesting unrelated scene changes.
Inspect the whole clip for identity drift, tracking errors and blending seams.

MiniMaxH3FrameInterpolation.purpose: Add in-between output frames and increase FPS while preserving duration.
MiniMaxH3FrameInterpolation.use: Prepare a smoother-rate delivery video after generation.
wiring: Decoded frames → images; matching audio → audio
steps: Enter the actual input FPS, normally 24 for H3 output.
Choose multiplier and available provider.
Keep cut detection on when the input includes scene cuts.
Encode at the returned FPS, not the original FPS.

examples.setup: Set fps=24 and multiplier=2, then encode at returned 48 fps.
examples.expect: Duration is preserved. Linear blends frames and can ghost; it is not learned optical-flow motion estimation.

notes: RTX provider needs its supported dependencies and hardware.
Using the original FPS after adding frames slows the video and breaks intended timing.
Interpolation cannot repair incorrect generated action or anatomy.
